sections.h2: What sets a Wildwood sale apart
sections.html:
Wildwood spreads across about 67 square miles at the western edge of St. Louis County, and that space shapes the market. Owners live in 91.8% of homes, the median owner-reported value is $495,800, and median household income is $161,060. Rentals are scarce, so most buyers plan to live in the house themselves. The July 2025 population estimate is 34,955, a little under the 35,417 counted in 2020.

Selling here means dealing with two layers of government. St. Louis County handles building records, inspections and tax bills, while the city handles zoning and, for rentals, occupancy permits. An owner-occupied sale needs no occupancy permit.

If you live in the house and sell it to someone who will live in it, you can skip this section. Wildwood's residential occupancy permit applies only to non-owner-occupied homes, under a program that took effect March 1, 2025. Whenever the occupant of a rental or other non-owner-occupied house changes, a permit and inspection are needed. New construction and owner-occupied homes need neither.

  • St. Louis County Public Works performs the inspection, and a passed inspection is not a permit by itself.
  • The application can go through the city's MyGov portal.
  • The inspection fee covers a first visit and a second one. Each extra visit costs $50.
  • An application lapses after 90 days if the noted deficiencies are not corrected.
  • The unit must be vacant when the inspector arrives.

This matters most if your buyer is an investor who plans to rent, since the new tenant has to wait for the permit. Metro West Fire Protection District also runs its own inspection within its service area. The Eureka and Monarch districts do not require one for single-family homes, but ask your fire district to confirm before you rely on that.

None of these fees land on an owner who sells to a buyer who will live in the house.

sections.h2: Permits and city rules that touch a property
sections.html:
Before closing, a buyer or seller who wants to change the house should start with the city's Planning Department at 16860 Main Street, phone 636-458-0440, which handles zoning authorization. Fences, decks, sheds, pools and retaining walls all need at least that. Building permits follow the St. Louis County code, and county Public Works takes calls at 314-615-2559.

  • Building permits cover additions, new construction, electrical and mechanical work, plumbing, structural changes, above-ground pools and some retaining walls.
  • Utility sheds of 120 square feet or less and fences under six feet skip the building permit but still need zoning authorization.
  • Grass over 10 inches counts as a nuisance under the city's code enforcement rules.
  • Trash bins must stay out of sight from the street in front of the house.

Utilities differ by address. Missouri American Water supplies water, MSD Project Clear provides sewer service, and trash pickup comes from Republic Services in urban areas or Gateway Disposal on rural and private roads. Residents 65 and older can ask their hauler for a 15 percent discount.

Buyers and investors will ask for paperwork, so line it up early. Begin with the county tax account and any permit history for decks, pools, sheds or retaining walls. The Planning Department can tell you whether earlier work carried zoning authorization.

  • Your fire district. Metro West, Monarch and Eureka cover different parts of the city, and only some inspect single-family homes.
  • Your trash hauler, Republic Services or Gateway Disposal, and whether you qualify for the 65-plus discount.
  • Who maintains your road. It may be Wildwood, St. Louis County, MoDOT or a neighboring city, and the Public Works office can point you to the right contact.
  • Your streetlight owner. The city maintains lights only in the Town Center Zoning District, and Ameren Missouri handles most others.

Put these facts in your listing so buyers know what service the address gets. The 2020 census counted 23.1 percent of residents as rural, which is part of why hauler and road answers vary from house to house.

St. Louis County manages every property tax bill in Wildwood. The Collector's office is in Clayton at 41 S. Central Avenue. Call (314) 615-7100, or (314) 615-7865 for back taxes. A payment or postmark by December 31 keeps a bill current. After that, interest of up to 18 percent a year plus a 2 percent penalty can apply under RSMo chapters 139 and 140.

If back tax is owed when you sell, the settlement statement should show it deducted from your proceeds. Ask for a payoff figure before the closing date.

The County Assessor revalues all real estate every odd-numbered year, so the next round is 2027. If you think a new value is too high, appeals go to the Board of Equalization. The window opens May 1 and closes the second Monday in July. A recent appraisal, a purchase contract or sales of similar houses give you something concrete to bring.

Some owners need a quick sale because of a move, an estate or repairs, and others have time to prepare. The usual paths are below.

  • List with an agent. Get the commission quoted in writing, and budget for repairs a buyer's inspector may raise.
  • Sell by owner. You control the price and the showings, and you also take on the contract and disclosures.
  • Sell to an investor. An investor may buy the house in its current state and close on your date. Compare the written offer with your likely net from a listing.

A cash sale skips the showings, the buyer's inspection negotiations and the wait for a lender, which can matter if you are on a deadline. It still goes through a title company, and any back tax or loan balance is paid from the proceeds.

faqs.q: Does Wildwood require an occupancy permit when I sell my home?
faqs.a: No, not for an owner-occupied home. The permit applies to non-owner-occupied properties when the occupant changes, under a program that began March 1, 2025.

faqs.q: How much is the Wildwood residential occupancy permit?
faqs.a: The city fee is $40, or $20 to update occupants. The inspection through St. Louis County is separate, and each visit after the second costs $50.

faqs.q: Which government bills property tax in Wildwood?
faqs.a: St. Louis County, through its Collector of Revenue in Clayton. Each year's bill is due by December 31.
Rockwood covers most of the city, and Lafayette High School is inside the city limits. A small corner belongs to the Meramec Valley district.

faqs.q: How high are Wildwood home values?
faqs.a: Owners reported a median of $495,800 for 2020 to 2024. Median household income is $161,060, and 91.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied.
